claim: Embryogenesis is an essential and stereotypic process that nevertheless evolves among species.
source: Embryogenesis is an essential and stereotypic process that nevertheless evolves among species.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about embryogenesis being both conserved and evolving.

claim: The essentiality of embryogenesis may favor the accumulation of cryptic genetic variation (CGV) that has no effect in the wild-type but that enhances or suppresses the effects of rare disruptions to gene function.
source: Its essentiality may favor the accumulation of cryptic genetic variation (CGV) that has no effect in the wild-type but that enhances or suppresses the effects of rare disruptions to gene function.
evidence: This is a theoretical speculation about the relationship between essentiality and CGV accumulation.

claim: The authors adapted a classical modifier screen to interrogate alleles segregating in natural populations of Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: Here, we adapted a classical modifier screen to interrogate the alleles segregating in natural populations of Caenorhabditis elegans
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: The authors induced gene knockdowns and used quantitative genetic methodology to examine how segregating variants modify the penetrance of embryonic lethality.
source: we induced gene knockdowns and used quantitative genetic methodology to examine how segregating variants modify the penetrance of embryonic lethality.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Each perturbation revealed CGV, indicating that wild-type genomes harbor myriad genetic modifiers.
source: Each perturbation revealed CGV, indicating that wild-type genomes harbor myriad genetic modifiers that may have little effect individually but which in aggregate can dramatically influence penetrance.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data showing CGV across all perturbations.

claim: Genetic modifiers may have little effect individually but in aggregate can dramatically influence penetrance.
source: wild-type genomes harbor myriad genetic modifiers that may have little effect individually but which in aggregate can dramatically influence penetrance.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of polygenic effects in the data.

claim: Phenotypes were mediated by many modifiers, indicating high polygenicity.
source: Phenotypes were mediated by many modifiers, indicating high polygenicity
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing multiple genetic contributors.

claim: The alleles tend to act very specifically, indicating low pleiotropy.
source: but the alleles tend to act very specifically, indicating low pleiotropy.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the specificity of modifier effects observed in the data.

claim: The average human genome contains loss-of-function alleles for 100 or more genes.
source: The average human genome contains loss-of-function alleles for 100 or more genes, some of which cause known genetic diseases
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies on human genomics.

claim: Disease expression depends on exposure of the disease allele and on variants elsewhere in the genome that act as penetrance modifiers.
source: disease expression depends on exposure of the disease allele, such as by homozygosity, but also on variants elsewhere in the genome that act as penetrance modifiers
evidence: This is supported by citation to published work on genetic modifiers.

claim: Genetic background effects are an example of cryptic genetic variation (CGV).
source: Genetic background effects are an example of cryptic genetic variation (CGV), the class of mutations that affect phenotype under rare conditions
evidence: This is a definitional statement based on established scientific knowledge and cited literature.

claim: CGV is invisible until a perturbation changes the molecular, cellular, or developmental processes that govern its phenotypic expression.
source: CGV is invisible until a perturbation changes the molecular, cellular, or developmental processes that govern its phenotypic expression.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about CGV based on established knowledge.

claim: CGV may be 'released' by environmental exposure, like modern changes to diet that have been hypothesized to underlie the emergence of complex metabolic diseases in humans.
source: In addition to genetic perturbations, CGV may be 'released' by environmental exposure, like the modern changes to diet that have been hypothesized to underlie the emergence of complex metabolic diseases in humans
evidence: This is supported by citation to published speculation about diet and disease.

claim: The concept of CGV has been of longstanding interest to evolutionary theorists because it explains how populations might store alleles that enable adaptation when conditions change.
source: The concept of CGV has been of longstanding interest to evolutionary theorists because it explains how populations might store alleles that enable adaptation when conditions change
evidence: This is supported by citations to historical evolutionary theory literature.

claim: Inhibition of the heat shock chaperone protein HSP90 reveals previously-silent mutational effects across many taxa.
source: Most of our empirical knowledge of CGV arises from studies that inhibited the heat shock chaperone protein HSP90 to reveal previously-silent mutational effects across many taxa
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published HSP90 studies.

claim: HSP90 inhibition probably represents a general mechanism that buffers genome-wide functional variation.
source: which probably represents a general mechanism that buffers genome-wide functional variation
evidence: This is an inference drawn from cited HSP90 studies.

claim: C. elegans embryogenesis is both complex and typically invariant.
source: C. elegans embryogenesis is both complex and typically invariant
evidence: This is established knowledge about C. elegans development.

claim: The complexity and invariance of C. elegans embryogenesis may favor the accumulation of mutations that act in a conditionally-functional manner.
source: C. elegans embryogenesis is both complex and typically invariant, which may favor the accumulation of mutations that act in a conditionally-functional manner
evidence: This is a theoretical speculation supported by citations.

claim: The authors revealed cryptic alleles by perturbing known embryonic genes and measuring differences in penetrance across multiple wild-derived strains.
source: We revealed these alleles by perturbing known embryonic genes and measuring differences in penetrance across multiple wild-derived strains.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Under ordinary conditions, wild-type C. elegans embryos hatch into larvae.
source: Under ordinary conditions, wild-type Caenorhabditis elegans embryos hatch into larvae.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A and stated in the text as established knowledge.

claim: The authors targeted maternally-expressed genes by RNAi to induce embryonic lethality that varied in penetrance across strains.
source: We targeted maternally-expressed genes by RNAi to induce embryonic lethality that varied in penetrance across strains.
evidence: This describes the experimental design shown in Figure 1B.

claim: L1 larvae in the parental generation were fed E. coli expressing dsRNA against target genes in 96-well plates in liquid media.
source: L1 larvae in the parental generation were fed Escherichia coli expressing dsRNA against target genes, in 96-well plates in liquid media.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 5 days after feeding RNAi bacteria, wells were imaged to capture the penetrance of embryonic lethality in the next generation.
source: 5 days later, wells were imaged to capture the penetrance of embryonic lethality in the next generation.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Raw images were evaluated using DevStaR, which identified objects as larvae, dead embryos, or adults.
source: Raw images were evaluated using DevStaR (White et al., 2013), which identified objects as larvae (blue), dead embryos (green), or adults (red).
evidence: This describes the image analysis method shown in Figure 1D and 1E, supported by citation.

claim: The experiments revealed extensive variation in embryonic lethality caused by genetic differences among strains.
source: The experiments revealed extensive variation in embryonic lethality caused by genetic differences among strains
evidence: This is a primary finding shown in Figure 2 and stated in the text.

claim: Each cell in Figure 2 represents the embryonic hatching success for a strain and targeted gene, averaged from at least eight replicate wells.
source: Each cell represents the embryonic hatching success for a strain and targeted gene, averaged from at least eight replicate wells.
evidence: This describes the data representation in Figure 2.

claim: Most strains exhibited moderately reduced lethality penetrance relative to the RNAi-sensitive laboratory strain N2.
source: Most strains exhibited moderately reduced lethality penetrance relative to the RNAi-sensitive laboratory strain N2
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Two strains, CB4856 and QX1211, showed consistently weak penetrance across the targeted genes.
source: but two strains, the germline RNAi-insensitive strain CB4856 (Tijsterman et al., 2002) and the genetically divergent strain QX1211, showed consistently weak penetrance across the targeted genes
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2, with citation for CB4856's known RNAi insensitivity.

claim: CB4856 harbors a ppw-1 loss-of-function mutation that confers resistance to germline RNAi.
source: CB4856 harbors a ppw-1 loss-of-function mutation that confers resistance to germline RNAi (Tijsterman et al., 2002)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: QX1211 and other strains with intermediate sensitivity do not harbor ppw-1 mutations based on sequencing.
source: but sequencing shows that QX1211 and other strains with intermediate sensitivity do not.
evidence: This is based on sequencing data generated in the study.

claim: A ppw-1 mutation in the N2 background was more sensitive than CB4856, showing high lethality on mex-3 and pos-1.
source: We found that a ppw-1 mutation in the N2 background was more sensitive than CB4856, showing high lethality on mex-3 and pos-1 (Figure 2)
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2.

claim: Some of the difference between N2 and CB4856 is ppw-1-independent.
source: indicating that some of the difference between N2 and CB4856 is ppw-1-independent.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of ppw-1 mutant in N2 background versus CB4856.

claim: Insensitivity to germline RNAi is genetically complex.
source: These results demonstrate that insensitivity to germline RNAi is genetically complex
evidence: This is an inference from the data showing variable RNAi sensitivity not fully explained by ppw-1.

claim: Wild C. elegans populations harbor many alleles affecting germline RNAi.
source: and that wild C. elegans populations harbor many alleles affecting germline RNAi (Elvin et al., 2011; Pollard and Rockman, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by the current study's data and cited previous work.

claim: Among wild-type strains, all but four (KR314, JU396, CB4852 and ED3040) showed complete sensitivity to somatic RNAi on tba-2.
source: Among wild-type strains, all but four (KR314, JU396, CB4852 and ED3040) showed complete sensitivity to somatic RNAi, indicated by developmental arrest of P0 animals on tba-2
evidence: This is an experimental observation from targeting tba-2.

claim: Most wild-type strains take up dsRNA and are capable of RNAi.
source: which demonstrates that most wild-type strains take up dsRNA and are capable of RNAi.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation of somatic RNAi sensitivity.

claim: An rrf-1 deletion mutant is sensitive to RNAi against genes expressed in the germline but resistant to RNAi in most somatic tissues.
source: An rrf-1 deletion mutant, which is sensitive to RNAi against genes expressed in the germline but resistant to RNAi in most somatic tissues (Yigit et al., 2006; Kumsta and Hansen, 2012)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The rrf-1 deletion mutant grew to adulthood but laid dead embryos on tba-2 RNAi.
source: grew to adulthood but laid dead embryos, suggesting that germline RNAi successfully silenced maternal tba-2 required for embryonic development.
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: The four somatically-resistant wild strains exhibited embryonic lethality on tba-2 and other germline-expressed genes.
source: The four somatically-resistant wild strains also exhibited embryonic lethality on tba-2 and other germline-expressed genes
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: The modifier variability acts tissue-specifically.
source: confirming that the modifier variability acts tissue-specifically.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that somatically-resistant strains still show germline RNAi effects.

claim: Gene-specific modifiers explain as much of the total variation as the informational modifiers, as estimated by the strain-by-gene interaction term.
source: Gene-specific modifiers explain as much of the total variation as the informational modifiers, as estimated by the strain-by-gene interaction term in our model (Table 1)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the model analysis.

claim: Gene-specific modifiers represent cryptic genetic variation in developmental processes.
source: and represent cryptic genetic variation in developmental processes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the statistical findings.

claim: The modifiers could act via network bypasses, where loss of the targeted gene reveals variation among strains in developmental network structure.
source: The modifiers could act via network bypasses, where loss of the targeted gene reveals variation among strains in developmental network structure (e.g., Zhang and Emmons, 2000).
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism supported by citation to an example.

claim: Gene-specific modifiers could act on the extent of the knockdown at a gene-specific level, resulting in variable residual activity of the targeted gene.
source: Gene-specific modifiers could also act on the extent of the knockdown at a gene-specific level, in a manner akin to intragenic suppressors, resulting in variable residual activity of the targeted gene.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism for how modifiers could work.

claim: Each of the 29 genes targeted showed significant strain-by-gene interaction coefficients.
source: Each of the 29 genes we targeted showed significant strain-by-gene interaction coefficients
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the analysis.

claim: Genetic modifiers of embryonic gene perturbations are pervasive in natural populations.
source: indicating that genetic modifiers of embryonic gene perturbations are pervasive in natural populations.
evidence: This is an inference from the finding that all 29 genes showed significant interactions.

claim: 36 gene pairs have known physical or genetic interactions.
source: 36 gene pairs have known physical or genetic interactions
evidence: This is based on information from wormbase.org as stated in the methods.

claim: Gene pairs with known interactions did not show significantly elevated phenotypic correlations (χ2 = 2.30, df = 1, p = 0.13).
source: but these did not show significantly elevated phenotypic correlations (χ2 = 2.30, df = 1, p = 0.13).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from correlation analysis.

claim: The average pairwise par gene correlation was no higher than the average correlation across all genes.
source: For example, despite high interaction within the par network, which underlies polarization of the zygote, the average pairwise par gene correlation was no higher than the average correlation across all genes (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from correlation analysis.

claim: Coefficients for par-3 and par-6 were correlated (correlation = 0.40, p = 0.003).
source: Coefficients for par-3 and par-6 were correlated (correlation = 0.40, p = 0.003)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from correlation analysis.

claim: Coefficients for par-3 and pkc-3 were not correlated (correlation = −0.17, p = 0.24).
source: but not for par-3 and pkc-3 (correlation = −0.17, p = 0.24)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from correlation analysis.

claim: Coefficients for par-6 and pkc-3 were not correlated (correlation = 0.12, p = 0.41).
source: or par-6 and pkc-3 (correlation = 0.12, p = 0.41)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from correlation analysis.

claim: PAR-3, PAR-6, and PKC-3 proteins together comprise the anterior polarity complex.
source: even though their proteins together comprise the anterior polarity complex (Munro et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The cryptic genetic modifiers have low developmental pleiotropy.
source: This indicates that the cryptic genetic modifiers have low developmental pleiotropy (Paaby and Rockman, 2013).
evidence: This is an inference from the low correlation between functionally related genes.

claim: Variation at cryptic loci must influence a very restricted suite of developmental events.
source: That is, variation at these loci must influence a very restricted suite of developmental events, since only specific perturbations uncover evidence of their phenotypic effects.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation of low pleiotropy.

claim: The high degree of redundancy observed in zygote polarization may explain the specificity of some factors.
source: For those associated with polarization of the zygote, this may be explained by the high degree of redundancy observed in the process (Beatty et al., 2010; Fievet et al., 2013; Motegi and Seydoux, 2013), as redundancy allows shared function of some factors and specificity of others.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation supported by citations to studies on redundancy.

claim: The low pleiotropy of cryptic alleles may be a result of purifying selection.
source: The low pleiotropy of cryptic alleles may be a result of purifying selection, which over evolutionary time should deplete populations of pleiotropic alleles as they may be more likely to be deleterious (Stern, 2000).
evidence: This is a speculative evolutionary explanation supported by citation.

claim: For most of the perturbations, variation in lethality penetrance is due to common alleles at many contributing cryptic loci.
source: We found that for most of the perturbations, variation in lethality penetrance is due to common alleles at many contributing cryptic loci.
evidence: This is an inference from the genomic heritability analysis.

claim: Of the 29 genes targeted, 12 exhibited gene-specific modifier variation with genomic heritability estimates greater than 0.80.
source: Of the 29 genes we targeted, 12 exhibited gene-specific modifier variation with genomic heritability estimates greater than 0.80
evidence: This is a statistical finding from heritability analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: For 19 genes, genomic heritability estimates were greater than 0.60.
source: for 19 genes, estimates were greater than 0.60 (Table 2).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from heritability analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: Genotypic similarity failed to explain phenotypic similarity for perturbations of emb-30, mel-32, mex-3, mom-5, par-3 and sur-6.
source: However, genotypic similarity failed to explain phenotypic similarity for perturbations of emb-30, mel-32, mex-3, mom-5, par-3 and sur-6 (Table 2).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from heritability analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: The genetic architecture of the cryptic variation associated with emb-30, mel-32, mex-3, mom-5, par-3 and sur-6 is likely comprised of few loci, rarer alleles, or both.
source: Thus, the genetic architecture of the cryptic variation associated with these genes is likely comprised of few loci, rarer alleles, or both.
evidence: This is an inference from the low heritability estimates for these genes.

claim: Nine of the 29 analyses identified at least one SNP associated with phenotype under a strict Bonferroni-corrected threshold for significance.
source: Nine of the 29 analyses identified at least one single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) associated with phenotype under a strict Bonferroni-corrected threshold for significance (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the genome-wide association analysis.

claim: A total of 19 SNPs or SNP haplotype blocks exhibited significant associations at the Bonferroni-corrected threshold.
source: Across all tests, a total of 19 SNPs or SNP haplotype blocks, defined by SNPs in high linkage disequilibrium (R2 > 0.9), exhibited significant associations at that threshold (Supplementary file 2)
evidence: This is a finding from the genome-wide association analysis.

claim: Introgression of part of chromosome II from strain N2 into strain EG4348 rescues the N2 phenotype on lsy-22 (F = 12.15, DF = 2, p = 0.001).
source: Introgression of part of chromosome II from strain N2 (yellow) into strain EG4348 (blue) rescues the N2 phenotype on lsy-22 (F = 12.15, DF = 2, p = 0.001)
evidence: This is an experimental validation shown in Figure 3.

claim: Introgression of part of chromosome II from strain N2 into strain EG4348 rescues the N2 phenotype on pkc-3 (F = 55.87, DF = 2, p < 0.001).
evidence: This is an experimental validation shown in Figure 3.

claim: Genome-wide analyses found associations between the introgressed chromosome II region and hatching phenotypes for both lsy-22 and pkc-3.
source: genome-wide analyses found associations between this region and hatching phenotypes for both lsy-22 and pkc-3.
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 3 caption and validates the GWAS findings.

claim: No SNPs lie within or near the locus of the targeted gene, with the exception of one SNP within the mel-28 locus that associates with the mel-28 phenotype.
source: No SNPs lie within or near the locus of the targeted gene, with the exception of one SNP within the mel-28 locus that associates with the mel-28 phenotype.
evidence: This is a finding from the genome-wide association analysis.

claim: Most of the CGV detectable by GWA is caused by extragenic modifiers.
source: Thus, most of the CGV detectable by GWA is caused by extragenic modifiers.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that most associated SNPs are not near target genes.

claim: Differences in severity of RNAi phenotype for four C. elegans strains perturbed at electron transport chain genes are associated with differences in expression level of the targeted gene.
source: Recent work shows that differences in severity of RNAi phenotype, for four C. elegans strains perturbed at electron transport chain genes, are associated with differences in expression level of the targeted gene (Vu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: The authors find no evidence for the pattern of lower expression explaining more severe phenotypes.
source: However, we find no evidence for the reported pattern of lower expression explaining more severe phenotypes.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of expression data.

claim: Five of the 29 target genes exhibited significant variation in expression among five strains.
source: Five of the genes exhibited significant variation in expression among the strains.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of published expression data.

claim: RNAi against 28 genes induced significant gene-specific variation in embryonic lethality among the five strains.
source: In contrast, RNAi against 28 induced significant gene-specific variation in embryonic lethality among the five strains.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: Lower expression of the target gene was usually correlated with less severe RNAi phenotypes (20 of 29 genes, p = 0.06).
source: Overall, both for genes with significant variation and for the whole set, lower expression of the target gene was usually correlated with less severe RNAi phenotypes (20 of 29 genes, p = 0.06)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from correlation analysis of expression and phenotype data.

claim: Much of the gene-specific modifier effect observed depends on variation beyond the target gene.
source: Although undetectable differences in transcript level may nevertheless contribute to embryonic survival, these results suggest that much of the gene-specific modifier effect we observe depends on variation beyond the target gene.
evidence: This is an inference from the weak correlation between expression and phenotype.

claim: GWA mapping identified few SNPs associated with more than one phenotype.
source: Our GWA mapping identified few SNPs associated with more than one phenotype.
evidence: This is a finding from the genome-wide association analysis.

claim: Lethality phenotypes for 4 of the 7 targeted polarity genes (par-2, -4, -6 and pkc-3) were associated with SNPs, but none were shared.
source: For example, lethality phenotypes for 4 of the 7 targeted polarity genes (par-2, -4, -6 and pkc-3) were associated with SNPs, but none were shared.
evidence: This is a finding from the genome-wide association analysis.

claim: The discrete nature of the genotype–phenotype associations implies low developmental pleiotropy of the cryptic alleles.
source: The discrete nature of the genotype–phenotype associations further implies low developmental pleiotropy of the cryptic alleles
evidence: This is an inference from the lack of shared SNP associations.

claim: Variants with effects under one perturbation have no detectable effects under another.
source: variants with effects under one perturbation have no detectable effects under another.
evidence: This is an inference from the specificity of SNP associations.

claim: rpn-9 and rpn-10 both encode non-ATPase regulatory subunits of the proteasome and are predicted to interact with each other.
source: as rpn-9 and rpn-10 both encode non-ATPase regulatory subunits of the proteasome and are predicted to interact with each other (Zhong and Sternberg, 2006; Lee et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: SNPs in a haplotype block on chromosome IV were significantly associated with lethality phenotypes for rpn-9 and rpn-10.
source: The co-association of SNPs in a haplotype block on chromosome IV with lethality phenotypes for rpn-9 and rpn-10 support a known relationship
evidence: This is a finding from the genome-wide association analysis.

claim: The chromosome IV haplotype was also significantly associated with lethality phenotypes for car-1, mom-5, and skn-1.
source: The haplotype, which spans approximately 10 kb, was also significantly associated with lethality phenotypes for car-1, mom-5, and skn-1
evidence: This is a finding from the genome-wide association analysis.

claim: skn-1 has a role in proteasome-mediated protein homeostasis.
source: skn-1 has a role in proteasome-mediated protein homeostasis (Li et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Modifier phenotypes for pkc-3 and rfc-3 are associated with SNPs on both chromosome III and X.
source: Separately, modifier phenotypes for pkc-3, involved in anterior-posterior polarity in the early embryo, and rfc-3, which shows homology to DNA replication factors C and effects on cell cycle synchrony (Piano et al., 2002), are associated with SNPs on both chromosome III and X.
evidence: This is a finding from the genome-wide association analysis.

claim: The co-associations of pkc-3 and rfc-3 with unlinked SNPs implicate the presence of at least two interacting cryptic alleles.
source: Because the co-associations occur twice, with unlinked SNPs (R2 = 0.26), they implicate the presence of at least two interacting cryptic alleles
evidence: This is an inference from the pattern of associations.

claim: The co-associations provide independent lines of evidence for a relationship between pkc-3 and rfc-3, genes with no reported interactions or shared functions.
source: and provide independent lines of evidence for a relationship between pkc-3 and rfc-3, genes with no reported interactions or shared functions.
evidence: This is an inference from the pattern of associations combined with knowledge of gene functions.

claim: The authors uncovered pervasive CGV that modifies the probability that an embryo will survive a gene perturbation.
source: We have uncovered pervasive CGV that modifies the probability that an embryo will survive a gene perturbation.
evidence: This is a summary of the primary finding from the experimental data.

claim: By evaluating the effects of naturally-occurring mutations on gene knockdowns, the authors explored a genotypic space that is distinct from that accessible to conventional screens.
source: By evaluating the effects of naturally-occurring mutations on gene knockdowns, we explored a genotypic space that is distinct from that accessible to conventional screens.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological approach of the study.

claim: The findings provide complementary insight, including discovery of modifier activity that may be detectable only when effects are moderate or polygenic.
source: Our findings provide complementary insight, including discovery of modifier activity that may be detectable only when effects are moderate (Fievet et al., 2013) or polygenic (Mackay, 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's contribution supported by citations.

claim: Without gene perturbation, the strains exhibit little embryonic lethality.
source: Without gene perturbation, our strains exhibit little embryonic lethality.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Under ordinary conditions the strains vary in gene expression and other cellular or developmental phenotypes.
source: However, under ordinary conditions the strains vary in gene expression and other cellular or developmental phenotypes (Grishkevich et al., 2012; Farhadifar et al., 2015)
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: Variation in gene expression and cellular phenotypes may be the mechanisms by which the cryptic alleles influence the penetrance of the primary perturbation.
source: which may be the mechanisms by which the cryptic alleles influence the penetrance of the primary perturbation.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism for how CGV operates.

claim: Whether a genetic variant is cryptic requires definition of the focal phenotype.
source: whether a genetic variant is cryptic requires definition of the focal phenotype
evidence: This is a conceptual statement about the definition of cryptic variation.

claim: An allele can be cryptic in one trait but penetrant in another.
source: since even at the morphological level an allele can be cryptic in one trait but penetrant in another (Duveau and Félix, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: CGV has been demonstrated following perturbation of candidate genes.
source: CGV has been demonstrated following perturbation of candidate genes (Gibson and Hogness, 1996; Dworkin et al., 2003; Cassidy et al., 2013; Chandler et al., 2013; Chari and Dworkin, 2013)
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: The potential role of CGV in adaptive evolution has been considered in diverse systems.
source: its potential role in adaptive evolution has been considered in diverse systems (Dobzhansky, 1941; Waddington, 1953; Masel, 2006; Ledon-Rettig et al., 2010; McGuigan et al., 2011; Duveau and Félix, 2012; Rohner et al., 2013)
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: CGV has been most extensively characterized following inhibition of HSP90.
source: and most extensively, it has been characterized following inhibition of HSP90 (Rutherford and Lindquist, 1998; Queitsch et al., 2002; Yeyati et al., 2007; Jarosz and Lindquist, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited studies.

claim: By systematic evaluation, the phenomenon of conditionally functional variation pervades even the highly stereotyped and controlled process of embryogenesis.
source: Here, we show by systematic evaluation that the phenomenon of conditionally functional variation pervades even the highly stereotyped and controlled process of embryogenesis.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the systematic experimental data.

claim: Gene-specific cryptic variation affects every targeted gene.
source: We found that gene-specific cryptic variation affects every targeted gene
evidence: This is a finding from the statistical analysis showing significant interactions for all 29 genes.

claim: Wild populations harbor many enhancers and suppressors of critical embryonic genes.
source: implying that wild populations harbor many enhancers and suppressors of critical embryonic genes.
evidence: This is an inference from the finding that all genes showed modifier variation.

claim: In humans, penetrance modifiers may mediate expression of genetic diseases arising from loss-of-function mutations.
source: In humans, such penetrance modifiers may mediate expression of genetic diseases arising from loss-of-function mutations (Abecasis et al., 2010; Hamilton and Yu, 2012; MacArthur et al., 2012)
evidence: This is a speculative application of the findings supported by citations.

claim: If the crypsis of penetrance modifiers is environmentally influenced, they may explain modern disease susceptibility.
source: and if their crypsis is environmentally influenced they may also explain modern disease susceptibility (Gibson, 2009).
evidence: This is a speculative application of the findings supported by citation.

claim: The screen revealed dramatic variation among wild-type strains in their responses to exogenous RNAi in the germline.
source: Our screen also revealed dramatic variation among wild-type strains in their responses to exogenous RNAi in the germline.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: Somatic RNAi response has been shown to influence C. elegans susceptibility to viral infection.
source: Somatic RNAi response has been shown to influence C. elegans susceptibility to viral infection
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited work.

claim: Variation in germline RNAi may affect vertical viral transmissibility.
source: variation in germline RNAi may affect vertical viral transmissibility (Félix et al., 2011)
evidence: This is a speculative implication supported by citation.

claim: Variation in germline RNAi may affect transposon activity.
source: as well as transposon activity (Sijen and Plasterk, 2003; Vastenhouw and Plasterk, 2004).
evidence: This is a speculative implication supported by citations.

claim: Conditionally-functional relationships between genes may pervade the variation on which natural selection acts.
source: The variation we describe illustrates how conditionally-functional relationships between genes may pervade the variation on which natural selection acts
evidence: This is a speculative evolutionary implication of the findings.

claim: Conditionally-functional relationships affect how complex traits evolve.
source: affecting how complex traits evolve (True and Haag, 2001; Félix, 2007; Wang and Sommer, 2011; Verster et al., 2014)
evidence: This is a speculative implication supported by citations.

claim: Conditionally-functional relationships affect the nature of complex trait genetic architecture.
source: and the nature of their genetic architecture (Mackay, 2014).
evidence: This is a speculative implication supported by citation.

claim: This variation has major implications for model system biologists that work with a single genetic strain.
source: Moreover, this variation has major implications for model system biologists that work with a single genetic strain.
evidence: This is an inference about the practical implications of the findings.

claim: The authors evaluated laboratory strain N2 and 54 wild-type strains derived from populations around the world.
source: We evaluated laboratory strain N2, originally derived from Bristol, England, and 54 wild-type strains derived from populations around the world.
